# X feed unit — SIEG X3.5D left table end (generated by feed_unit.py)

**Status: concept with PLACEHOLDER mill dimensions.** Measure the items in docs/mill.md, edit the
`F` dataclass at the top of `feed_unit.py`, re-run, and check the renders before cutting metal.

## Drive
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Belt | HTD 5M, 295 mm (59 T), 15 mm wide |
| Pulleys | 20 T (PD 31.83) on the clutch output Ø12; 40 T (PD 63.66) on the Ø15 stub → 2.0:1 |
| Centre distance | 70.71 mm, tension slot ±3 mm along the centre line |
| Module position | 70.7 mm from the leadscrew at -90° (below) |
| Belt plane | 23.0 mm out from the bracket face |
| Overall | ≈262 mm out from the table end (housing end panel) |

Firmware: `belt_ratio = 2.0`, `encoder_counts = 2400` (per leadscrew turn; the encoder is on the stub).

## Parts to make
| Part | Material | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Plate | 6061, 28 mm, CNC | **Ø32 H7 straight through**: too big to swing on the lathe (300 mm needed), so bore it on the mill with a boring head. DIN 472-32 grooves (Ø33.7 × 1.3) leaving a **2.6 land** at each face: keyseat cutter (head ≤ Ø28, 1.0–1.2 wide, two passes) by circular interpolation, one face, then flip for the other. Clutch-module hole slotted Ø40 and 4× Ø5.5 slots (±3): 5×D deep, cut them from both faces. 4× Ø6.6 for the standoffs; 3× M3 × 8 deep on r=23 (encoder posts, outer face); 2× M5 × 12 for the tension block. Edge holes (M3 × 8 for the housing): stand the plate in the vise on its edge, or use a drill-guide block. Corners R9 |
| Standoffs | steel or 6061 | 4× Ø14 × 35, Ø6.6 thru (M6 screws into the table end) |
| Leadscrew stub | steel, turned from **Ø20** stock | from the table side: tongue 4.8 × 14 × 4 (across the Oldham slot), Ø15 with a 0.6 flat for the 40T set screws, **Ø18 × 2 shoulder** on the inner bearing's inner race (corner radius ≤ 0.3 so the bearing's chamfer clears it), Ø15 h6 at both bearings with **Loctite 641 on the inner one** (as on the clutch; easier than holding k6 and h6 bands on a manual lathe), DIN 471-15 groove (Ø14.3 × 1.1) just outboard of the inner bearing, Ø8 × 10 encoder end |
| Bearing spacer tube | steel or 6061 | Ø31.95 / Ø28 × 1.8, between the outer races. The inner bearing locates the stub (shoulder + DIN 471-15 either side of it); the outer one floats on the stub |
| Oldham disc | steel (1045) or bronze (CuSn12), greased — acetal creeps at the ~45 MPa of a stall/cam-out | Ø24 × 9: tongue 14 × 3.8 on one face (into the leadscrew slot), cross slot 5.0 wide × 4.5 deep on the other. Takes up to ~1 mm offset between the plate and the leadscrew, and end float |
| Encoder disc | 6061, 5 mm | Ø50 with a flat 20 from centre toward the clutch module; Ø22 centre hole; 3× Ø3.4 on r=23 (posts) and 3× Ø3.4 on r=15, 60° offset (encoder, **check your encoder's hole circle**) |
| Encoder posts | 3× M3 hex standoffs F-F, 21 mm | |
| Tension block | steel | 44 × 14 × 12 on the plate's outer face below the module, 2× M5 to the plate; M4 drawbolt through it into a radial M4 tapped 7 deep in the cover's front wall (bottom, between two module bolts). Tighten the drawbolt to tension the belt, then lock the 4 module bolts |
| Belt guard | PETG print | a cup: closed back against the table end (Ø28 pass-through for the leadscrew and Oldham disc), open face covered by the plate; captured between the two |

## Assembly
1. Plate: outer circlip, outer 6002 (pressed in from the chamber side), spacer tube.
2. Stub: inner 6002 against the shoulder, DIN 471-15 behind it. Push the stub through the outer bearing from the
   chamber side (support the outer bearing's inner race) until the inner bearing seats, then the inner circlip.
3. Encoder to its disc, coupling on the encoder shaft, disc onto the posts, coupling onto the stub end.
4. 40T pulley on the stub (set screws on the flat), Oldham disc on the stub tongue, guard into the chamber, then
   the plate onto the standoffs: the Oldham tongue goes into the leadscrew slot.
5. Clutch module through the plate's slotted hole, 20T pulley and belt, 4 module bolts finger-tight, drawbolt to tension, lock.
   The bolt heads are on the chamber side, outside the guard outline: reach them from the side with a ball-end key.

## Buy
- HTD 5M pulleys 20 T and 40 T for 15 mm belt (re-bore to Ø12 / Ø15 H7).
- Belt 295-5M-15.
- 2× 6002-2RS, 2× DIN 472-32, 1× DIN 471-15.
- Flexible coupling 6 × 8 mm (encoder).
- LPD3806-600BM-G5-24C encoder.
- 4× M6 for the standoffs; 4× M5×35 + washers for the clutch module (28 plate + 8 wall: the tips stop clear of the hub); 2× M5×20 (tension block) + 1× M4×30 (drawbolt); 3× M3 hex standoffs 21 mm and 6× M3×8.

## Notes
- The module hangs ≈177 mm off the plate on 4 M5 into the cover. The cover's spigot over the clutch housing is
  18 mm long with 6 radial M4, so the motor is held stiffly. A strap from the motor's tail to the
  table end is optional if the mill vibrates a lot.
- The chamber (35 mm) is set by the Oldham disc plus the belt plane: the 40T pulley's inner flange clears the stub tongue.

## Housing: the whole power feed in one compact box (3D printed)
The drive, the controller PCB and the controls share one rounded housing on the table end. Outside it there is
only the belt chamber (closed by the guard cup), the 36 V supply and the limit switches. The housing carries no load
(the aluminium plate carries the bearings, the module and the belt), so it is printed.

Packing: the clutch and motor hang below the leadscrew, the encoder sits on the leadscrew next to the plate, the
**PCB lies flat above the motor** (components up, connector edge toward the end wall), and the controls sit in a
strip along the upper front with their bodies reaching back over the PCB.

| | |
|---|---|
| Outer size | 116 (front-back) × 190 (high) × 207 mm (along the table); long edges R12, the top-front edge and the end wall chamfered 45° (they lie on the print bed); plus the 35 mm belt chamber and the controls proud of the front |
| `shell` (one print) | back, bottom, end and lower-front walls (3 mm), the rails, the 4 PCB bosses, the louvre block. **Print standing on the end wall**, 207 mm tall (MK3S: 210). Every boss and block has a 45° underside, so **no supports**; only short bridges (≤ 12 mm: rail windows, louvre slots). PETG, 4 perimeters, 20 % gyroid |
| `hood` (one print) | top + control strip, one L-shaped piece. **Print with the strip face down**: the engraved labels come out crisp on the bed side; its back lip has a 45° inside so it prints without support. Lift it off and the whole PCB is exposed from above |
| Plate | aluminium, 110 wide, bottom corners R9, both top corners chamfered 10.5 × 45° to sit under the housing's chamfered inside |
| Fixing | both prints overlap the plate edges by 8 mm with 0.25 mm clearance per side, and screw into them (15× M3×8 countersunk into tapped holes); the hood also takes 9× M3×8 into heat-set inserts (M3 × 5.7, Ø4.0 holes) in the shell's rails |
| PCB | on 4 printed bosses (heat-set inserts, M3×6), underside -33 mm below the leadscrew axis, ≥ 3 mm above the motor even with the motor raised 3 mm by the belt tensioner. The rails above it have 12 mm windows over all 4 holes, so a screwdriver and the insert iron go straight down (checked). Trim the SWD header's (J3) pins flush underneath. Air rises past the board between the bosses |
| Plugs | J1/J2/J5 MSTB plugs (≈13 mm) + ferrules: the wires run toward the end wall and turn down past the board's edge, behind the motor tail (19 mm), checked with a plug + wire-bend envelope. Unplugging in place: slide the plug off, the wires have slack below |
| Controls (strip, left → right as you face it) | E-stop (Ø60 legend ring fits on the flat face), LEFT/STOP/RIGHT toggle over RAPID, SPEED dial with the OLED above it; adapter board (2×7 IDC) on the strip's inside, ~200 mm ribbon down to J6 so the hood can be lifted and set beside the unit |
| End wall | 2× M16 cable glands **low**, beside the motor (36 V on the J1 side, limit switches on the J7 side). **Programming ports, usable with the box closed:** a Ø16 hole for a round nut-mount USB-C panel extension (e.g. Adafruit #6069; its male end stays in J4, plug body ≤ 12.4 × 6.6) and a recessed **SWD port** (1×3 0.1" header, SWCLK / GND / SWDIO like J3, pressed into the slot from outside with a drop of CA; solder 3 wires to its inner pins and run them to J3) |
| Vents | intake slots in the bottom under the motor; exhaust through a louvre block high on the back wall, beside the encoder (slots climb 45° inward through 7.5 mm, so chips can't fall in), away from the fuse. The block takes a 40 mm fan (4× M3 self-tapping, 32 mm square) on its inside |

- **Programming with the box closed:**
  - **Normal update:** settings menu (long-press the dial while stopped) → last item **USB FLASH** → hold: the RP2040
    reboots into its USB drive (`RPI-RP2`); copy `power-feed.uf2` onto it through the end-wall USB-C.
  - **Recovery, any state (blank, crashed, bad build):** Raspberry Pi Debug Probe on the end-wall SWD port (its
    JST-to-0.1" cable), then `cargo run --release` in `firmware/feed-app` (probe-rs flashes, resets and shows logs).
    The 36 V supply must be on (the probe doesn't power the board), or USB-C power is enough for the logic.
- **Fuse:** lift the hood.
- **Heat:** the motor is inside and the PCB sits above it. Default run current 3 A (~16 W in the coils), 1 A at standstill.
  PETG's glass transition is ~80 °C; the walls are ≥ 5.8 mm from the motor. On the bench, run it closed for 30 min:
  if the motor case passes ~60 °C, fit the 40 mm fan (exhaust), lower `MOTOR mA` in the menu (light feeds need far
  less), or reprint in ASA (needs an enclosure on the MK3S to print without warping).
- **Order:** plate (bearings, stub, module, encoder) → slide the shell over the module onto the plate edges, screw it
  on → heat-set inserts → PCB onto its bosses → wire the motor, clutch and encoder up behind the motor tail → glands →
  fan (optional, it covers the H1 hole's tool path: fit it after the PCB) → hood with its controls last.
- **Possible next size cut:** the floor is set by the belt-tension block under the clutch; behind it (from W ≈ 130)
  the floor could step up ~35 mm, under the motor. Not done yet.

## PLACEHOLDERS (measure, then edit `F`)
- `screw_d`, `screw_end_slot_w`, `screw_end_slot_d`, `screw_end_z`: the left leadscrew end and its drive slot.
  - If there is no slot, use a pinned sleeve coupling instead of the tongue.
- `standoffs`: where M6 can go into the table end or the left bracket.
- `motor_angle_deg`: rotate the module if it hits the saddle, the base or the DRO cable at full travel.
- The housing reaches -6 mm in front of the table's front edge (E-stop head included) and 143 mm below the
  leadscrew: check both against the saddle, the DRO reader and the base at full right travel.
- `chamber`: the minimum is set by the clutch output shaft; the script asserts it fits.
